input.summary: Design a bounded emulated-netem pilot to test whether adding 20 ms one-way delay changes TCP flow completion time under fixed bottleneck conditions. Two clients, two CCA configurations (with/without delay), cubic CCA. Protocol is null pending three owner decisions on directionality, file size, and bottleneck rate.
clarification_questions: Should the 20 ms delay be applied as one-way (client-to-server) or round-trip (both directions), and what is the intended bottleneck link rate in Mbit/s for the emulated test?
What file transfer size(s) in MBytes should each client use, and should both clients use the same size or different sizes?
Which TCP congestion control algorithm(s) should be tested (e.g., cubic, bbr, reno), and is a single CCA sufficient for this pilot or should multiple CCAs be compared?

proposal.problem: The claim asserts that adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions. The direction of the effect (increase or decrease), the bottleneck rate, file sizes, and CCA are unspecified in the source metadata.
proposal.question: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, does adding 20 ms delay change TCP flow completion time, and if so, in which direction and by how much?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two conditions: (1) baseline — no added delay, fixed bottleneck; (2) treatment — 20 ms delay added (direction unresolved), same fixed bottleneck. CCA, file size, and bottleneck rate are unresolved owner decisions.
proposal.related_work: The source is a synthetic networking paper claim provided for development evaluation; no full text or prior measurements are available. No external citations are introduced.
proposal.alternatives: Alternative explanations include: (a) the delay effect is too small relative to bottleneck-induced queuing delay to be detectable; (b) the direction of the effect depends on CCA-specific behavior (e.g., BBR vs. cubic); (c) buffer size at the bottleneck mediates the observed change.
proposal.design: Independent-check emulated pilot using netem_nines.py with two clients. One configuration applies zero added delay (control); a second applies 20 ms delay (treatment). Flow completion time in ms is the primary metric. Replications are proposed at 8 per configuration to allow descriptive comparison.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: flow_completion_time_ms (ms) per client per replication. Comparison: median and range across replications for delay vs. no-delay conditions.
proposal.controls: Bottleneck rate, buffer size, loss rate (0%), CCA, file size, and number of clients are held fixed across conditions. Only the added delay varies between treatment and control.
proposal.falsification: The claim is not supported if the distributions of flow_completion_time_ms under 0 ms and 20 ms delay conditions overlap substantially and no consistent directional shift is observed across replications. A recorded zero FCT is retained, not excluded.
proposal.inputs: Required: owner decisions on bottleneck rate (Mbit/s), file size (MBytes), CCA, and delay direction (one-way vs. round-trip). Source sha256: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa. Context sha256: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb.
proposal.limitations: Source is synthetic with no full text; coverage is recorded metadata only. The pilot uses emulation (simulation), not real-world hardware. Results cannot establish causality or generalize beyond the tested configuration. Three owner decisions remain unresolved; protocol is null until resolved.
